title: Initiative
theme: Enterprising behaviours, proactive workplace action, teamwork, and responsibility

overview.tagline: Scan the five initiative signals, clear the gate, then prove them through a chosen applied mission.
overview.playerFantasy: Enter a workplace mission reactor where initiative must be recognised, applied, and proven before rewards unlock.
overview.teacherValue: Separates active time from learning impact by gating choice behind the Unlock Gate, tracking applied mission proof, and requiring a Memory Vault recall check.

gameplayIdentity.playStyle: intel scan followed by structured student agency

learningObjectives: Define initiative as proactive action that contributes positively to the workplace.
Identify five ways workers show initiative: being proactive, improving work practices, vocalising opinions, helping fellow workers, and seeking more responsibilities.
Classify workplace examples and non-examples of initiative.
Apply initiative to a chosen creative, interview, journal, scenario, or occupation-based pathway.
Produce teacher-visible evidence that explains why an example shows initiative and how it helps the workplace or team.

sharedStatEffects.description: Initiative supports workplace contribution, promotion readiness, and employability.
Workers who act early, solve problems, and support others become more valuable in workplaces.
Strong initiative can contribute to promotion, responsibility, and future earning potential.
Applied evidence contributes to the wider class learning economy once completion is proven.

employabilityFocus.whyItFits: Students must vocalise ideas, explain evidence, and communicate initiative examples clearly.
Initiative is strongest when it supports team goals, safety, and shared workplace productivity.
Being proactive and improving work practices require noticing problems and proposing practical responses.

activities.title: Intel Scan
activities.purpose: Introduce the definition and five behaviours using the one-page summary and mini video.

activities.title: Unlock Gate
activities.purpose: Gate applied learning until the student can identify the five behaviours and definition.

activities.title: Scenario Judge
activities.purpose: Classify examples of initiative and explain the workplace effect.

activities.title: Song Remix
activities.purpose: Use creative repetition while protecting accurate curriculum language.

activities.title: Proof Drop
activities.purpose: Require every pathway to produce the same curriculum evidence before completion.

assessmentEvidence.prompt: Identify the definition and five ways workers can show initiative.
Use a chosen pathway to apply initiative accurately.
Define initiative, identify a behaviour, explain why it is initiative, and describe the workplace or team effect.
Complete a post-pathway retention check on the five initiative behaviours.

teacherSignals: core checkpoint attempts and best score
support signal: mastery, performance-driven, low self-efficacy, overwhelmed, avoidant, or hopelessness
